Town meeting!

The Popular Dēmokratia of Potamosia convenes an ASSEMBLY OF THE PEOPLE. All citizens of Potamosia are hereby summoned to the Central Plaza on Wednesday afternoon for the duration of a half-hour Sand Timer. Attendance, participation, and voting is mandatory for all adult citizens. Failure to comply will result in a 3-Drachma fine. On the agenda:

Public spending on construction projects

There are three proposed projects:

1. Building a dam would prevent river floods and provide water reserves for agriculture.
2. Building a bridge would make traveling around town easier.
3. Building city walls would protect the city from outsiders.

According to the meeting notes of a previous assembly, Coffers Guardian testifies that the city only has enough gold to cover the cost of one of these projects. By Law, spending gold from the city coffers requires a vote in the assembly.

Per section λγ12 of Potamosia city’s charter,

“Two citizens, chosen by lot, shall serve as co-chairs of the Assembly, empowered to grant the floor, draft resolutions, and call votes. Should the Sand Timers of an assembly meeting run out with no law enacted, the co-Chairs will hereby be exiled for Life from the city of Potamosia.”

As is our custom, the assembly will be opened with a presentation of information regarding the projects on the agenda by the mayors.*

See you Wednesday!

BE THERE OR BE FINED

ASTERISK: Potamosia has two mayors, whose job is to ensure the smooth management of the town, its treasury, and council meetings. Mayoral elections take place once a year, where any citizen may stand for election and the two candidates with the most votes win, so long as they each have a majority of votes. There are no term limits to mayors and current mayors have been in office for most of the last ten years. Mayors may be impeached by the assembly at any time.

Council Meeting!

The Council of the Worthy convenes in the Central Plaza

The Wise Council of Hudrosia shall convene a COUNCIL MEETING at the Central Plaza on Wednesday afternoon. Councillors are required to attend; all citizens may come and observe.

On the agenda:

Public spending on construction projects

There are three proposed projects:

1. Building a dam would prevent river floods and provide water reserves for agriculture.
2. Building a bridge would make traveling around town easier.
3. Building city walls would protect the city from outsiders.

The city reserve only has enough gold to cover the cost of one of these projects.

The Council of Hudrosia — the Kings, the Merchants, and the Nobles — shall deliberate for twenty sand-minutes and its decision is made by consensus. In the ten sand-minutes that follow, the Kings shall present the Council's decision to the assembled city, and answer what questions the people may raise.

BY ORDER OF THE TWO KINGS — LET THE COUNCIL DECIDE

Hudrosia has two kings, who together run the council: they draft the proposals, moderate the discussion, and solicit advice from whomever they choose. The kings are the hereditary heads of the two oldest families who founded the town, and the role passes from generation to generation rather than by election. There are no term limits, and by custom a proposal backed by both kings has never failed to be accepted by the council.

Emergency Town meeting!

The Popular Dēmokratia of Potamosia convenes an emergency ASSEMBLY OF THE PEOPLE. All citizens of Potamosia are hereby summoned to the Central Plaza on Wednesday afternoon for the duration of 30 minutes. Attendance, participation, and voting is mandatory for all adult citizens. Failure to comply will result in a 3-Drachma fine. On the agenda:

Credible reports: intensive warship production in Hudrosia

There are three proposals:

1. Launch a surprise attack on Hudrosia to defeat them before they can strike at us.
2. Divert resources from essential services to invest in defences that would repel an invasion.
3. Engage in diplomacy: send envoys hoping to find common ground and ease tensions.

In recent years the tensions around the meadow between the cities and Potamosia’s Great Dam have heightened, resulting in repeated and escalating clashes. In the past year, Hudrosian raiders have been attacking our shepherds as they graze Potamosia’s historic meadow. In addition, our people have discovered and foiled several attempts to sabotage Potamosia’s Great Dam, which would be catastrophic. The mayors have convened an urgent assembly meeting following worrying reports regarding intensive warship production in Hudrosia, suggesting they are gearing up for an attack.

Per section λγ12 of Potamosia city’s charter,

“Two citizens, chosen by lot, shall serve as co-chairs of the Assembly, empowered to grant the floor, draft resolutions, and call votes. Should the Sand Timers of an assembly meeting run out with no law enacted, the co-Chairs will hereby be exiled for Life from the city of Potamosia.”

As is our custom, the assembly will be opened with a presentation of information regarding the alternatives on the agenda by the mayors.*

See you Wednesday!

BE THERE OR BE FINED

ASTERISK: Potamosia has two mayors, whose job is to ensure the smooth management of the town, its treasury, and council meetings. Mayoral elections take place once a year, mayors are elected by a majority of votes. There are no term limits to mayors and current mayors have been in office for most of the last ten years. Mayors may be impeached by the assembly at any time.

The Council of Hudrosia — the Kings, the Merchants, and the Nobles — shall deliberate for twenty minutes and its decision is made by consensus. Citizens are invited to observe the council’s deliberation. Following the meeting, the Kings will present the Council's decision to the assembled city, answering questions and responding to comments for 10 minutes.

BY ORDER OF THE TWO KINGS — LET THE COUNCIL DECIDE

Hudrosia has two kings, who together run the council: they draft the proposals, moderate the discussion, and solicit advice from whomever they choose. The kings are the hereditary heads of the two oldest families who founded the city, and the role passes from parent to child in those families. A proposal backed by both kings has never failed to be accepted by the council.
